skill.name: pr-dev-acceptance
skill.description: Validate human-approved Bitbucket pull requests on existing development deployments against Jira requirements. Produce browser evidence, fresh-login persistence checks, and local acceptance reports.
skill.summary: Verify approved development deployments through browser acceptance tests, fresh logins, and saved screenshot evidence.
skill.author: alvolutionor

remediation.suggestion: Retain the existing test-data restrictions and add a pre-upload checklist for visible secrets and personal information.

remediation.suggestion: Use least-privilege service accounts and restrict access to the private configuration file and credential environment variables.

content.value_statement: Teams need evidence that approved changes work on the existing development deployment. This skill guides browser checks, verifies persistence after fresh login, and delivers reports with screenshots.
actual_capabilities: Guides verification of human Bitbucket approval, approved commits, and existing deployment identity.
Derives focused browser cases from Jira requirements and the approved diff.
Exercises real application routes and verifies persistence through independent fresh logins.
Creates local Markdown acceptance reports with saved, inspected screenshots.
Converts Markdown comments to Jira markup and previews planned attachments.
Uploads screenshots, posts comments, and optionally transitions Jira issues when explicitly requested.
limitations: It does not deploy code or start, rerun, or resume pipelines.
It requires an existing development deployment and authorized test accounts.
It depends on external browser tools, fresh-login access, screenshot saving, and verifiable deployment evidence.
Jira helper preview requires network access and credentials; writes require explicit authorization and the apply option.

use_cases.title: Release acceptance
use_cases.description: Validate an approved pull request against Jira requirements before release handoff.

use_cases.title: Product verification
use_cases.description: Confirm changed user flows, roles, and saved results on an existing development deployment.

use_cases.title: Audit-ready handoff
use_cases.description: Produce a concise report with approval, deployment identity, test results, and screenshot links.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic acceptance check
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the approved pull request against the linked Jira requirements on the existing development site. Report blockers before testing.

prompt_templates.title: Test a changed user flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test the approved change for the supplied role and route. Record the expected result, observed result, persistence check, and relevant screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Verify deployment identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the approved source commit is present in the deployed development application. Use read-only evidence and stop if the deployment cannot be linked.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare the Jira handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Jira comment from the completed acceptance evidence, including results, test-data notes, and screenshot references. Inspect the helper preview without applying writes.

output_examples.input: Validate the approved profile update pull request on the development site.
output_examples.output: BLOCKED: The deployment identity could not be linked to the approved commit. No acceptance result was issued.

output_examples.input: Run the authorized checkout cases and verify the saved order in a fresh login.
output: PASS: Checkout and saved-order cases matched the requirements.
Evidence: The final fresh session confirmed the saved order and included readable screenshots.
Handoff: A local Markdown report records the approval, deployment identity, routes, roles, and results.

best_practices: Use dedicated test accounts and project-approved records.
Record deployment identity before and after testing.
Inspect saved screenshots and preview Jira content before any authorized post.
anti_patterns: Do not test an unapproved commit or an unverified deployment.
Do not use production data, invented credentials, or synthetic screenshots.
Do not deploy, change code, or post Jira updates without explicit authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy the pull request?
faq.answer: No. It tests an existing development deployment and reports missing or incorrect deployment evidence.

faq.question: What approval does it require?
faq.answer: It requires human Bitbucket reviewer approval for the source commit under the repository rules.

faq.question: Why is a fresh login required?
faq.answer: A fresh session verifies that the result persists beyond the original browser state and test actions.

faq.question: Can it use production accounts?
faq.answer: No. Use dedicated project-approved development accounts and records.

faq.question: Does it post to Jira automatically?
faq.answer: No. The helper previews by default, but still reads Jira using credentials. Posting requires explicit authorization and the apply option.

faq.question: What happens when access is missing?
faq.answer: The affected case is marked blocked, with the missing prerequisite recorded in the report.
